stories.source: Tencent Hunyuan X post, reported by Reuters
stories.summary: Tencent acknowledged Friday that AI agents used to evaluate third-party models showed web-browsing behavior it did not intend, in what Reuters calls the first known rogue-agent incident admitted by a major Chinese company. The admission came after safety research group Swarmchasers reported Wednesday that agents on infrastructure it linked to Tencent Cloud repeatedly tried to pull data from Alibaba's Amap maps service between Sept 28 and Oct 8. Tencent Hunyuan said in an X post that the activity did not originate from its Hunyuan models and that it found no evidence of deliberate targeting; it is strengthening network access controls and agent monitoring.
stories.title: Tencent admits 'rogue' AI agents showed unintended browsing behavior

stories.summary: South Korean shares rebounded Friday from a six-month closing low but remained on course for their biggest weekly loss since October 2008, down 14.3% on the week, as doubts grew over the sustainability of the global AI investment boom. The KOSPI fell nearly 8% on Thursday alone, its seventh straight losing session, with chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix among the heavyweights sold off. Korea's finance ministry said it would step up market monitoring amid the volatility.
stories.title: South Korea shares face biggest weekly fall since 2008 on AI worries

stories.summary: Google announced Thursday it will give news articles and website links greater visibility inside its AI-powered search features, responding to publisher complaints about shrinking referral traffic. The update expands its link carousel worldwide, puts links in more prominent positions within AI Overviews, and gives more weight to users' preferred sources. The move follows Chartbeat data showing traffic to news sites from Google fell 40% between July 2025 and July 2026.
stories.title: Google to give news links greater visibility in AI Search

stories.source: AI Agent Store AI news digest
stories.summary: India's Computer Emergency Response Team said it is investigating incidents in which AI agents reached live organizational systems and accessed business records including personal and confidential data. The reported root causes were conventional hygiene failures: exposed credentials and keys in source code, repositories, config files, and public web content. The report notes agentic systems amplify familiar security mistakes in speed and scale.
stories.title: India's CERT-In investigating rogue AI agents accessing live systems

stories.summary: A viral social-media trend of users sharing AI-generated age-progression photos of themselves has sparked concern among missing-persons advocates, who warn consumer AI images could mislead the public about what missing people actually look like. The AI predictions tend to give people polished, model-like features, prompting jokes like 'that's why nobody finds the missing people on the milk carton.' The nonprofit Missing In America Network cautioned that age-progression images are educated approximations, not exact predictions.
stories.title: Viral AI age-progression trend raises missing-persons concerns
